ideas: Something specific about the company's product or mission
Evidence you've done research: a customer story, a blog post, the product
How your skills match what they need now

phrases.phrase: I'd love to be part of

learn.explain: This question tests whether you did your research and whether you're choosing this company or just any job. Generic answers, "it's a big company with a good culture", are a red flag. A strong answer names something specific: the product and what makes it different, a customer case study you read, a blog post or talk by the team, the company's values in action, or the stage of the company. Then connect it to yourself: a relevant project, the type of customers you'd like to work with, or a skill they need. Prepare this fresh for each company. In this pack the example uses an AI company; replace the details with real research.
points: You name one or two specific things, proving real research.
You link them to your own experience or interests.
You show what you'd contribute, not only what you'd gain.
mistakes: Generic praise that could apply to any company.
Talking only about salary, brand or benefits.
Getting facts about the company wrong, which is worse than being general.

framework.starter: What stood out to me was…
That lines up with my experience, because…
I'd love to be part of… and help…

betterWays.weak: Your company is big and famous.
betterWays.strong: What stood out to me was how your team works directly inside customers' systems, not just selling a tool.
betterWays.why: Specific to how the company works.

betterWays.strong: I read your engineering blog post about the logistics customer, and I liked that you described the mistakes too.

betterWays.weak: I want to learn from the best.
betterWays.strong: I'd learn a lot here, and I think I can contribute quickly on integration work, because I've done it before.

betterWays.weak: Your product is very good and useful.
betterWays.strong: I tried the free version and built a small assistant for my university's FAQ in an afternoon.
It's not just about AI being popular; I want to help companies actually get value from it, which is the hard part.
betterWays.why: A thoughtful reason instead of a trend.

model: What stood out to me was how your company works with customers. A lot of AI companies sell a tool and leave the customer to figure it out. You put engineers inside the customer's business, and that's the part of the work I care about most. I came across your blog post about the logistics customer, where your team cut their support backlog by half, and what I liked was that you also wrote about what didn't work at first. That honesty made me want to know more. So what I did was try the product myself. I built a small assistant for my university's student FAQ in an afternoon, and as a result I got a feel for both what's powerful about it and where a real customer would need help, like connecting it to their own documents. That lines up with my experience. In my internship I built tools for a logistics operations team, so I've seen first-hand how messy real processes are. It's not just about AI being popular; the hard part is helping a company actually get value from it. I'd love to be part of the team that does that, and I think my integration experience means I can contribute quickly.
short: What stood out to me is that you put engineers inside customers' businesses instead of just selling a tool. I read your post about the logistics customer and liked that you included what didn't work. I tried the product and built a small FAQ assistant in an afternoon. With my logistics internship, I've seen first-hand how messy real processes are, and I'd love to help customers get real value.

followUps.q: Who do you think our main competitors are?
followUps.answer: From what I've read, the main competitors are the other large AI labs and some consulting firms that build on top of them. I think your difference is the combination of a strong model and engineers who deploy it, but I'd be curious how you see it.

followUps.q: What would you change about our product?
followUps.answer: From my short experience, connecting it to existing documents took me the longest. A simpler setup for that would help smaller customers a lot. But I'd want to understand your customers better before suggesting anything seriously.

followUps.q: Are you applying to other companies?
followUps.answer: Yes, a few, mostly for similar customer-facing engineering roles. But this is the one I'm most excited about, because of how directly your engineers work with customers.

selfCheck: I named something specific about the company.
I showed evidence of research or first-hand use.
I linked it to my own experience.
I said what I would contribute.
I answered the follow-up without restarting a sentence.
